title: The Mistake Everyone Makes About Noah's Ark #shorts #bible
description:
The Bible never says Noah's Ark landed on Mount Ararat. Not once.

Genesis 8:4 says only "the mountains of Ararat", and Ararat was a kingdom, Urartu, around Lake Van. The oldest Jewish translation, the Targum Onkelos, says the mountains of Qardu. The Babylonian priest Berossus, as quoted by Josephus, placed the ship's remains in the Gordyaean mountains. The Quran names al-Judi. Many scholars place all three around Mount Cudi in southeastern Turkey.

So... Ararat or Cudi? Or do you think Noah's Ark really existed? Comment REAL or MYTH.
Subscribe to Or So The Story Goes for more history mysteries, told from the sources.

Sources: Genesis 8:4; Targum Onkelos, Genesis 8:4; Berossus via Josephus, Antiquities of the Jews I.93; Quran, Surah Hud 11:44.
